description: Eight sessions of errands in the fictional town of Milldale. The arcs: recurring facts reward recall; two later corrections force prune-then-recreate; a weekend-hours fact routes to EXTEND; a paraphrased duplicate exposes an honest false-CREATE; two distinct riverside concepts share vocabulary and must not merge; one note carries a deliberately lazy hook that causes a shown retrieval miss; one one-off note decays. 'relevant' lists ground-truth notes for precision/recall and refers only to notes existing before the task runs. 'intended' is the ground-truth routing for the write-back confusion table.

tasks.prompt: What time does the bakery in Milldale open tomorrow?
tasks.answer: The bakery at 21 Main Street opens at 7am on weekdays and closes at 3pm.

learnings.title: bakery-hours
learnings.hook: Opening hours for the Milldale bakery on Main Street
learnings.body:
Opens 7am weekdays at 21 Main Street.
Closes 3pm.

tasks.prompt: How do I walk from the square to the school?
tasks.answer: Take Main Street north two blocks from the square, then Oak Lane east to the school gate.

learnings.title: town-map
learnings.hook: Layout of Milldale: which streets cross and where the square sits
learnings.body:
Main Street runs north from the square.
Oak Lane crosses east at the second block.
The bakery sits on Main Street — see [[bakery-hours]].
learnings.reason: walked the route and mapped it

learnings.title: school-play
learnings.hook: One-off: the school play happening this week
learnings.body: The school play runs this week only, in the gym, evenings.
learnings.reason: poster seen on the school gate

tasks.prompt: When does the bakery open on Tuesday?
tasks.answer: Weekday opening is 7am, so Tuesday it opens at 7am.

tasks.prompt: Which bus goes to the library and how do I get a library card?
tasks.answer: Route 4 stops by the library; bring one piece of mail to the counter to get a card. The Saturday market poster was up at the stop.

learnings.title: library-card
learnings.hook: How to get and renew a Milldale library card
learnings.body:
Bring one piece of mail to the counter.
Renew every two years, free.

learnings.title: bus-schedule
learnings.body:
Route 4 hourly from the square, 7am to 8pm.
Stops at the library and Elm Street.

learnings.title: farmers-market
learnings.hook: The Saturday farmers market on the town square
learnings.body:
Saturdays 8am to noon on the square.
Produce, bread, and cider stalls.
learnings.reason: poster seen at the bus stop

tasks.prompt: What bus can I take to the farmers market on Saturday?
tasks.answer: Route 4 runs hourly from the square; the market is on the square Saturdays 8am to noon, so any morning route 4 works.

tasks.prompt: Where can I get my bike fixed and is there a pharmacy nearby?
tasks.answer: The bike shop on Forge Alley does repairs with a two-day turnaround; the pharmacy is on Elm Street, open 9am to 6pm. The riverside park was worth the detour after.

learnings.title: pharmacy-hours
learnings.hook: Hours for the pharmacy on Elm Street
learnings.body:
Open 9am to 6pm weekdays on Elm Street.
Closed Sundays.

learnings.title: bike-repair
learnings.hook: The bike shop on Forge Alley: services and turnaround
learnings.body:
Repairs with a two-day turnaround on Forge Alley.
Tubes and brake work done same day.

learnings.title: riverside-park
learnings.hook: The riverside park: picnic tables and walking trails
learnings.body:
Picnic tables by the water and two walking trails.
Quietest before noon.

tasks.prompt: Is the pharmacy on Elm Street open this evening?
tasks.answer: The note says 9am to 6pm weekdays, so it is closed this evening after 6pm.

tasks.prompt: What time is the last route 4 bus and which streets does it cross?
tasks.answer: Route 4 runs until 8pm from the square, along Main Street past Elm. An old-town leaflet was in the rack at the stop; the bakery window also had weekend hours posted.

learnings.title: town-history
learnings.body:
The old mill by the river was founded in 1851 by the Harlan family.
The town charter dates to 1863.
learnings.reason: leaflet picked up at the bus stop; hook written lazily on purpose

tasks.prompt: When does the bakery open on Saturday?
tasks.answer: Saturday hours are 8am to 1pm, per the extended note.

tasks.prompt: Is the farmers market running this Saturday and where is it?
tasks.answer: Yes — Saturdays 8am to noon on the town square.

tasks.prompt: Where can I park near the river for a picnic?
tasks.answer: The picnic tables are in the riverside park; the gravel lot off River Road has free parking, forty spaces.

learnings.body:
Gravel lot off River Road, free, forty spaces.
Fills by mid-morning on market days.

learnings.reason: sign read while passing the clinic

tasks.prompt: How do I renew my library card this month?
tasks.answer: Renewal is free every two years — bring one piece of mail to the counter.

tasks.prompt: Which bus route runs past the riverside park?
tasks.answer: Route 4 from the square passes Elm Street near the river; the park entrance is a short walk from that stop.

tasks.prompt: Can I still catch the route 4 bus by the square tonight?
tasks.answer: No — the town notice posted today says route 4 is discontinued; a new route 7 now runs from the square. The walk-in clinic sign by the stop listed Saturday hours too.

learnings.title: walk-in-clinic-hours

learnings.reason: same clinic as the existing note — a paraphrased title the exact matcher will miss, counted as false-CREATE

corrections.reason: contradicted by session 6 town notice: route 4 discontinued

replacement.title: bus-route-7
replacement.body:
Route 7 hourly from the square, 7am to 9pm.
Replaces route 4 — see [[town-map]] for the streets it crosses.

tasks.prompt: When was the old mill by the river founded?
tasks.answer: No note matched this question, so it cannot be answered from memory.

tasks.prompt: Is the pharmacy on Elm Street still open until 6?
tasks.answer: The note says 9am to 6pm — but the new owner posted new hours today: 8am to 8pm every day. The note is now wrong and gets pruned.

tasks.prompt: What is happening at the harvest festival and where is the mayor's office?
tasks.answer: The harvest festival runs the first weekend of the month on the square; the mayor's office is on the second floor of the town hall, open Monday to Thursday.

First weekend of the month, on the square.
Cider pressing, stalls, and a lantern walk.

learnings.body:
Town hall, second floor.
Open Monday to Thursday, 10am to 4pm.

tasks.prompt: When does the bakery open today and is the hardware store open too?
tasks.answer: The bakery opens 7am weekdays, 8am Saturday; the hardware store on Forge Alley turned out to be open 8am to 6pm.

learnings.title: hardware-store
learnings.hook: The hardware store on Forge Alley: stock and hours
learnings.body:
Open 8am to 6pm, Monday to Saturday.
Stocks paint, tools, and stove parts.

tasks.prompt: Which route 7 bus gets me to the harvest festival?
tasks.answer: Route 7 runs hourly from the square, and the festival is on the square itself — any morning bus works.

tasks.prompt: Can the bike shop fix a flat tire before the clinic opens?
tasks.answer: Tube work is same-day at the bike shop; the clinic opens at 9am on weekdays (both clinic notes describe the same clinic — the duplicate is the cost of the missed merge).
